title: Power Automate Process Mining: analyse processes with object-centric process mining
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, ingestion requirements, licensing figures and capacity allocation references are supported. The capacity API is present in the cited tutorial despite the automatic pre-check warning; the Fabric administrator role statement needs an additional citation.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: OCPM analyzes interacting business objects such as orders, deliveries and invoices rather than forcing each event into one case ID.
claims.quote: Object-centric process mining (OCPM) analyzes processes by following the real objects that interact

claims.claim: OCPM records events related to multiple objects and object types in one process.
claims.quote: OCPM models that reality by recording events that relate to many objects and object types in one process, preserving their relationships end-to-end.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The ingestion page directs makers to store the object-centric event log as a CSV in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote: Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.claim: The maker selects Process mining > Start here, then Object-centric process mining.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane to the left, select Process mining > Start here.
2. Select Object-centric process mining.

claims.claim: Mapping requires one Activity attribute.
claims.quote: You must map one attribute of type Activity.

claims.claim: Mapping requires one Start event attribute.
claims.quote: You must map one attribute of type Start event.

claims.claim: Mapping requires at least two Object type attributes.
claims.quote: You must map at least two attributes of type Object type.

claims.quote: After the ingestion finishes, you're navigated to the process intelligence experience for OCPM with the Process overview tab active.

claims.quote: The Process Map is a central visualization showing the process flow across multiple objects

claims.claim: Process overview includes object counts.

claims.claim: Process overview includes a process analysis widget.
claims.quote: Process analysis provides detailed statistical analysis based on the leading object and an optional path

claims.claim: Process overview visuals respond to filters.
claims.quote: All visuals in the Process overview react to the selected filter criteria.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.where: controls[1]; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No OCPM-specific admin UI or API on/off switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: object-centric process mining disable enable tenant setting API; object-centric settings disable; object-centric production-ready. Opened OCPM overview, ingest, process overview, Power Platform tenant-settings and settings-features; no OCPM-specific switch found.

claims.claim: No change is documented for users who do not build process mining models.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object centric process mining existing processes users automatic changes. Opened OCPM overview, ingest, process overview and semantic model; no change for non-builders documented. The ingestion workflow starts with explicitly creating a process.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment makers can create, share and contribute to processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Object-centric event logs carry object IDs.
claims.quote: each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Event and object attributes, including financial attributes, are optional but highly recommended.
claims.quote: Event and Object level attributes (including financial) are optional but highly recommended for more detailed analysis

claims.claim: Access to the exported Fabric model and lakehouse copy is governed by Fabric permissions rather than Power Automate process permissions.
claims.quote: Workspace roles are used to control access to workspaces and the content within them.

claims.claim: Stored process data consumes capacity, mostly file capacity.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity. ... The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process mining access relies on environment security and Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators and system customizers can access every process in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires sharing the Fabric workspace with the Process Insight Prod service principal as Admin.
claims.quote: The Fabric workspace needs to be shared to the Process Insight Prod service principal with an Admin role.

claims.claim: The user performing initial Fabric workspace setup for the environment needs the Admin role.
claims.quote: The Admin role must be attributed to the user performing the initial workspace setup for the environment for the other users in the same environment.

claims.claim: No autonomous business actions are described for OCPM.
claims.quote: Searched: object-centric process mining autonomous. Opened object-centric-overview, object-centric-ingest-event-log, object-centric-process-overview and object-centric-semantic-model; documented operations are ingestion, analysis, refresh and optional export, not autonomous business actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; writer evidence
claims.claim: Publishing to Fabric creates a DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to it.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.

claims.claim: Refresh Data in the analytics overview triggers full ingestion and creation of the process model.
claims.quote: Refresh Data: Button to reload and refresh the displayed analytics with the most recent data (this action triggers the full ingestion and creation of the process model).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining per-user Power Automate Premium capacity and a tenant-wide Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license ... The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each Power Automate Premium licence adds 50 MB to a tenant-wide process mining capacity pool.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: The process mining capacity accumulated from Premium licences is capped at 100 GB per tenant.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: At the 100 GB threshold, additional process mining capacity requires the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: When you reach 100 GB, you need to purchase the Power Automate Process Mining add-on to process more data.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide licence available for Power Automate Premium.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on adds 100 GB to the process mining capacity pool.
claims.quote: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: The add-on adds 2 GB of Dataverse database capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 2 GB of Dataverse database capacity.

claims.claim: The add-on adds 1 TB of Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 1 TB of Dataverse file capacity.

claims.claim: The FAQ lists the Process Mining add-on at $5,000 for 100 GB of data stored per month.
claims.quote: List Price (USD): $5,000 for 100 GB of data stored/month

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium is a required prerequisite for the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: Required prerequisite: Power Automate Premium. Multiple add-ons can be applied to a single prerequisite.

claims.claim: The FAQ says to purchase capacity for peak utilization over a 12-month contract period.
claims.quote: Capacity should be purchased for the peak utilization over a 12-month contract period.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Customers can assess their highest monthly process mining usage in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Yes, customers can assess their highest monthly Process Mining usage to understand capacity needed. Current and past usage data are available in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Power BI licences are not included in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: Power BI licenses aren't included in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The OCPM pages name no separate licence or meter, and no separate OCPM meter is published.
claims.quote: Searched: object-centric process mining licensing meter price; object-centric process mining license premium. Opened OCPM overview, ingest, process overview, semantic model, process-advisor-overview and Power Platform licensing FAQ; no separate OCPM licence or meter found.

claims.claim: OCPM is a Power Automate Process Mining capability subject to its process mining capacity pool.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: The exported semantic model is created on Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.
claims.quote: The semantic model is created on top of Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.

claims.claim: OneLake lakehouse storage is billed pay-as-you-go per GB.
claims.quote: OneLake storage is billed at a pay-as-you-go rate per GB of data used and doesn't consume Fabric Capacity Units (CUs). Fabric items like lakehouses and warehouses consume OneLake storage.

claims.claim: OneLake reading and writing requests consume Fabric Capacity Units.
claims.quote: Requests to OneLake, such as reading or writing data, consume Fabric Capacity Units.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires a Fabric workspace other than My workspace.
claims.quote: A Fabric workspace that's different from the default My workspace.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to Fabric to be switched on.
claims.quote: Ensure that Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to the Fabric option is switched on in the OneLake tenant settings.

claims.claim: OneLake event logs must already be in final event-log format because post-ingestion transformation is unavailable.
claims.quote: All data must be in final event log format ... Data should be ready to be mapped to the process mining schema. No data transformation is available post ingestion.

claims.claim: The generic capacity allocation UI path is Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Summary > Add-ons > Manage.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... select Capacity add-ons. ... select the Summary tab. ... Scroll down to the Add-ons section, and select Manage.

claims.claim: The tutorial documents PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2022-03-01-preview for allocating add-ons.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Patch -Uri "https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/$EnvironmentId/allocations?api-version=2022-03-01-preview"

claims.claim: The current Currency Allocation reference lists ProcessMiningDataStorage as an allocatable environment currency.
claims.quote: ExternalCurrencyType ... The available currency type that can be allocated to an environment. ... ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: The generic capacity allocation UI page does not explicitly identify the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: Searched: Process Mining and process mining in the full capacity-add-on page; read its allocation procedure and examples. Also opened programmability-tutorial-allocate-capacity-addons and the Currency Allocation reference; the UI page does not name Process Mining.

claims.claim: The internal Process Mining Application role must not be assigned to users.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses. ... Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application roles.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: The current Currency Allocation reference documents API version 2024-10-01, unlike the tutorial's 2022-03-01-preview.
claims.quote: PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: A Fabric administrator configures the OneLake tenant setting in Fabric.
claims.quote: These roles provide access to the admin experience in Govern and control over organization-wide Fabric settings, usage metrics, and admin features, except for licensing.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/admin/roles to sources for the Fabric administrator role statement; keep the existing OneLake tenant-settings citation.

claims.claim: No OCPM-specific audit or activity events for creation, ingestion and sharing are documented.
claims.quote: Searched: object-centric process mining audit activity log creation ingestion sharing; Power Automate Process Mining audit logging process create share ingestion Purview. Opened OCPM documentation and activity-logs-power-automate; no OCPM creation, ingestion or sharing events found.

claims.claim: Microsoft's OCPM ingestion page labels the linked Fabric semantic model export documentation as preview.
claims.quote: Export OCPM semantic model into Fabric workspace (preview)
